newsitem.title: FRANCE: French post office in non-life talks with AGF.
newsitem.headline: French post office in non-life talks with AGF.

text.p: AGF shares rose after the French post office said on Wednesday it was talking to the French insurer and other potential partners about a deal to distribute non-life insurance products through its 17,000 outlets.
"Consultations are under way with different possible partners, among them AGF," La Poste said in a statement.
La Poste issued the statement after the daily Le Monde reported that AGF would create with Sofiposte, the body overseeing the post office's subsidiaries, a company to market specific products.
The company would have turnover of 3 billion francs ($517 million) and be operational at the end of 1999, the newspaper said.
"They are contacts (with La Poste), no more than contacts," said an AGF spokesman. "We know there are other contacts with other companies."
AGF shares finished up 5.80 francs at 176.30 francs.
The French insurer already has had dealings with La Poste. It designed its highly successful Valorea life insurance product which La Poste marketed for a year through its Arcalais unit.
La Poste also sells life insurance products through state-owned Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance.
An accord with the insurance industry which ended in 1992 restricted La Poste from distributing non-life insurance products.
Le Monde said a deal on distributing life insurance products was near but it would have to be approved by the Finance Ministry "which is far from being automatic".
It said the sale by La Poste of non-life insurance products would be hotly opposed by other insurance companies which would fear the competition.
The deal would give the post office's chosen partner a unique market network in France. ($ = 5.8 French Francs)
